subject: Scope & success metrics — pilot readiness checklist (Greenfield Labs)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Scope & success metrics — pilot readiness checklist (Greenfield Labs)

Hi Emma — thanks again for a productive discovery call this morning. Below is a concise recap and proposed kickoff plan so we can align on scope, success metrics, owners, and required access before the pilot starts.

Top pain points you shared
- Search relevance degrades on longer documents (especially legal/terms PDFs)
- Token cost spikes during large-batch reranking runs
- Intermittent hallucination on entity extraction from noisy OCR text

Objectives for a successful pilot
- Fix: reduce hallucination rate on entity extraction to < 20% on the evaluated prompt set
- Latency: p95 inference latency < 300ms for 512-token generation in our topology
- Cost: demonstrate ≤ 40% per-token cost reduction vs your current baseline via batching + KV caching

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks)
1) Data: ingest up to ~1M doc records (sample subset first) into a staging S3 bucket; we will not persist PII outside your VPC.
2) Models: Redwood hosted model A (quantized) + fallback model B (higher-accuracy) for canary routing.
3) Eval: 250 labelled prompt-eval pairs (seed set attached) for precision/recall and hallucination checks.
4) Ops: latency & cost dashboards enabled; daily token breakdown.

Owners & roles
- Redwood: Grace O'Connor (engagement PM), Ben Carter (SRE/solutions lead)
- Greenfield: Emma Blake (Product Owner), Carlos Mendez (Infra/Cloud)

Immediate access asks
- Provision an AWS staging S3 bucket and grant the service account (redwood-greenfield-integ) read/object-list permissions
- Short-term key for KMS access or a gateway NAT if you require no KMS handoff
- Sample export: 5k documents (redacted) uploaded to s3://greenfield-staging/sample-5k

Attachments included: greenfield_mutual_action_plan.xlsx, prompt_set_seed_v1.jsonl

Next steps (please confirm by EOD Thurs):
- Greenfield to confirm kickoff window: suggested Mon 2026-11-15 for a 30–45m technical kickoff
- Greenfield to start security questionnaire (I attached the security stub; Ben can help drive)
- Redwood to draft sprint plan and measurement dashboard before kickoff

If that all looks right, I’ll send a short mutual-action-plan and calendar invite for 11/15.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Engagement Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Grace — that readout is helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few quick clarifications: 

- SOC2 / compliance: before we move data into any third-party service, we need a SOC2 Type II attestation and an outline of data retention & deletion processes. Can your security team share the latest attestation?
- KMS: we prefer to manage keys in our account (KMS). Is there an agent or gateway option for your private deployment to respect our KMS?
- Sample data: we can provide the 5k redacted set by EOD Monday. Carlos will provision an S3 bucket and share the ARN.

I’ll loop in Carlos for infra specifics. If possible, please include a rough estimate for expected spend during the 4-week pilot (order-of-magnitude).

On the kickoff date, 11/15 works for me but we need Carlos present for provisioning signoff.

—Emma
Emma Blake
Head of Product, Greenfield Labs
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@greenfield.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scope & success metrics — pilot readiness checklist (Greenfield Labs)

Hi Emma / Carlos — quick technical responses from my side: 

- SOC2: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II; I’ve attached the security questionnaire (redwood_security_questionnaire.pdf) and can send the attestation PDF via your vendor portal once you confirm the contact email.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and a KMS-KMS envelope approach for Dedicated. For the hosted pilot we can use a customer encrypted upload to S3 (you manage keys) + a short-lived service token on our side. We can walk through options on the kickoff call.
- Network: VPC peering is not required for the initial pilot; an S3 presigned approach is fine for staged ingestion. If you prefer VPC endpoints, we’ll need the route / CIDR details ahead of time.

Cost: order-of-magnitude for the pilot (staging + eval runs) is approximately $6k–$12k depending on eval volume and whether you run continuous reranking. We’ll produce a more refined estimate after understanding exact qps and batch sizes.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b-greenfield-pilot (I placed a runbook + sample infra policy).

Happy to take the security questionnaire and set an internal owner for it — Grace or I can own follow-ups.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_security_questionnaire.pdf]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Emma Blake <emma@greenfield.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Scope & success metrics — pilot readiness checklist (Greenfield Labs)

Great — thanks for the fast responses, both. Two quick clarifications and the proposed milestone plan below.

Evaluation & success criteria (concrete)
- Quality: On the 250 eval pairs we’ll measure exact-match, precision/recall for entity extraction and a hallucination metric (manual adjudication). Target: precision ≥ 0.80 and hallucination ≤ 0.20.
- Latency: p50/p95 targets (p95 < 300ms) measured on a 95/5 production-like traffic mix.
- Cost: show per-token unit economics and at least one configuration that reaches ≤ 40% of your current baseline.

Prompt / eval ownership
- Greenfield to supply the 250 labelled eval pairs and the 5k redacted sample (Emma/Carlos)
- Redwood to seed a prompt bank and produce variations; we’ll coordinate on edge cases during week 1.

Proposed 4-week sprint milestones
Week 0 (pre-kickoff): security questionnaire complete, S3 bucket created, pilot access token provisioned
Week 1: data ingestion + baseline runs (sanity checks)
Week 2: prompt/eval tuning; initial quality runs and short A/B between model A/B
Week 3: scaling tests, latency tuning, and cost optimization (batching/caching)
Week 4: final evaluation, runbook handoff, and recommendations presentation

Action items (owner)
- Emma: confirm 11/15 kickoff & provide S3 ARN (by 11/10)
- Carlos: provision bucket + KMS guidance (by 11/10)
- Grace: send mutual action plan and calendar invite (today)
- Ben: security questionnaire follow-up and cost estimate (by 11/12)

I’ll attach a short mutual-action-plan after this message and put calendar invites on behalf of the team. If Greenfield prefers a different timeline, we can shift to a 6-week cadence to leave more time for labelling.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—Grace
